# Summary of Philip Rubin
Philip Rubin is an accomplished researcher and leader whose interdisciplinary work spans psychology, linguistics, engineering, physiology, and computational modeling, particularly focusing on speech and language. Educated at Brandeis University (BA, 1971) and the University of Connecticut (PhD, 1975), Rubin is best known for pioneering articulatory synthesis and sinewave speech synthesis technologies developed primarily at Haskins Laboratories. His influential programs include ASY (articulatory synthesis), CASY (configurable articulatory synthesizer), and SWS (sinewave synthesis), which advanced modeling of speech production, perception, and multimodal communication. Rubin contributed theoretical frameworks using dynamical systems approaches to speech and emphasized the embodiment and temporal coordination of speech gestures. He was core leader of the NIH-funded research project on speech code acquisition and helped found the Auditory-Visual Speech Association (AVISA).
Beyond scientific contributions, Rubin has held numerous leadership roles in science administration and policy. He served as Chair of the National Academies Board on Behavioral, Cognitive, and Sensory Sciences (2006-2011), Director of NSF’s Division of Behavioral and Cognitive Sciences (2000-2003), and Assistant Director at the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy (2012-2015), where he led initiatives in neuroscience, research policy, human subjects protection, and open data. He is President and Chair of the Federation of Associations in Behavioral and Brain Sciences (FABBS) and has been active in ethics and oversight of emerging technologies, including critiques of unproven security tools and human subjects research regulations. Rubin has also been involved with organizations such as iGIANT, NASA Advisory Council panels, and university governance at the University of Connecticut and Haskins Laboratories, where he currently chairs the Board of Directors. He has received multiple fellowships and awards recognizing his research and leadership in speech science and behavioral sciences.
